content.title: Atletico Madrid 1-2 Barcelona: La Liga – as it happened
content.text: 10 Apr 2026 - 16:30 (16:30 GMT)FIFA opens disciplinary probe against Spanish FA after Islamaphobic chantsWorld football’s governing body, FIFA, has opened disciplinary proceedings against the Spanish football federation over anti-Muslim chants heard at a recent match between Spain and Egypt.A section of fans at the RCDE stadium in Barcelona had chanted, “Whoever doesn’t jump is a Muslim”, during the international friendly on March 31.“FIFA has opened disciplinary proceedings today against the Spanish FA for the incidents in the friendly against Egypt,” the governing body said in a statement on Tuesday.It was the latest in a string of similar incidents to overshadow Spanish football in recent years, with Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior in particular repeatedly racially abused.Last week, Spanish police said they were investigating “Islamophobic and xenophobic” chants, and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez condemned an “unacceptable” incident while insisting that an “uncivil minority” would not be allowed to tarnish the country.4 Apr 2026 - 21:49 (21:49 GMT)That’s a wrapBarcelona maintain their stranglehold on first place with a narrow 2-1 result over a spirited Atletico side.They will hope their seven-point gap is enough to clinch the title over their perennial archrivals, Real Madrid.We hope you enjoyed this pulsating encounter. From Kevin Hand and me, Rohan Sharma, thank you for joining us.4 Apr 2026 - 21:42 (21:42 GMT)Next up for Al Jazeera SportWe shift our focus to the upcoming Champions League quarterfinals next.Bayern Munich and Real Madrid lock horns at the Bernabeu on April 7, with the live blog set to kick off at 16:00 GMT.4 Apr 2026 - 21:38 (21:38 GMT)Flick: ‘After the red card, we controlled the match, and we deserved the win’Barcelona manager Hansi Flick dissected the match: “Lamine [Yamal] was a bit angry, because he was trying everything and didn’t score.“It’s an emotional match; that’s normal. He’s back in the locker room now, and he’s fine.“After the red card, we controlled the match, and we deserved the win.“On Wednesday, we play them again, and it will be very tough. We need to play our game, give everything, and prepare for the match.“We’re in a good position; eight matches left and seven points clear on top.“We tried everything to score the last goal. It was not easy. The atmosphere, the emotions, were running high. It was very difficult, and I’m happy for the three points.”4 Apr 2026 - 21:32 (21:32 GMT)Musso: ‘Eleven against eleven; we were the better side’Atletico Madrid goalkeeper Juan Musso, who was awarded the MVP of the match for his brilliant saves to keep his side close, shared his thoughts: “We were better than Barcelona in the first half.“After that, they gave us [Nicolas Gonzalez] the red card. In today’s football, you can’t compete with a player less.“It was a red card for them as well [for Eric Martin, which was later rescinded]. I can tell you that. The ref had the correct call since the beginning.“Eleven against eleven; we were the better side. We move on, and this match has given us confidence. I trust this team.”4 Apr 2026 - 21:31 (21:31 GMT)Read all about it: Our Barca-Atletico report is liveClick here to read our full report from the match in Madrid.4 Apr 2026 - 21:26 (21:26 GMT)Garcia: ‘We knew that winning today was going to be a statement’Barcelona defender Eric Garcia spoke with LaLigaTV after the match: “We knew what had happened in this stadium in the Copa del Rey.“We knew that winning today was going to be a statement.“It’s difficult to attack a team that sits so deep.”4 Apr 2026 - 21:20 (21:20 GMT)A look at the standingsBarcelona go seven points adrift in top spot, with 76 points after 30 matches completed.Real Madrid, having lost to Mallorca 2-1 earlier in the day, sit in second, with 69 points.Villarreal continue to inhabit third, with 58 points, with Atletico in fourth at 57 points.Sign up for Al JazeeraBreaking News AlertGet real-time breaking news alerts and stay up-to-date with the most important headlines from around the globe.4 Apr 2026 - 21:14 (21:14 GMT)Updated match day 30 resultsWith half of the matches wrapped up, here are the updated results: Rayo Vallecano 1-0 Elche Real Sociedad 2-0 Levante Mallorca 2-1 Real Madrid Real Betis 0-0 Espanyol Atletico Madrid 1-2 Barcelona 4 Apr 2026 - 21:08 (21:08 GMT)Lewandowski’s late goal downs 10-men AtleticoAfter losing Gonzalez deep in the first half, it looked like the door was unlocked for Barcelona to run rampage in Madrid.But the hosts defended resolutely, despite constant attack, to take the match deep into the 87th minute.A chance deflection off a Cancelo cross ended up sinking the hosts’ hopes of preserving a draw, with Lewandowski’s shoulder pushing the Calatans into the lead.Full-time: Atletico Madrid 1-2 Barcelona
